scope: Read-only generic RRF implementation/configuration audit; no original acceptance question text or per-question outcomes read.
testCodeRead: Only constructor/configuration call lines found with rg in K03RetrievalLiveTest.java; no frozen question file or individual acceptance result opened.

findings.evidence: RagRetrievalService two-argument convenience constructor fixes k=60/candidates=100; NativeRagService constructor uses that path. Spring configureRetrieval setter replaces it with the @Value-configured bean. Live test manually constructs NativeRagService and currently has no setter/configuration call.
findings.impact: Changing environment variables/properties alone does not tune that non-Spring fixture. Parameterized service must be explicitly constructed/injected. Production Spring configuration is wired.

findings.kind: No generic mathematical implementation defect found
findings.evidence: Vector matches are descending cosine with stable id ties; positive BM25 and vector rank lists are separately capped, absent channel contributes zero, final score equals reciprocal-rank sum and sorted descending.
findings.limits: Not a claim RRF improves this corpus, nor a semantic quality acceptance.

findings.kind: Expected consensus bias with large candidate pools and k
findings.evidence: For k=60 and at most 50 rows present in both lists, minimum double-channel score 2/(60+50)=0.0181818 exceeds best single-channel score 1/61=0.0163934. Broad positive cosine candidates and weak lexical overlap can therefore outrank a strong match present in only one channel.
findings.impact: Candidate size above a small corpus is effectively no truncation. RRF discards raw BM25/cosine magnitude; this is an algorithm tradeoff, not a wrong sum or missing-rank bug.
findings.limits: Synthetic arithmetic examples are not recommended tuned values; choose parameters only on frozen tuning questions.

findings.evidence: Lexical score<=0 means no BM25 contribution; semantic-only candidates remain allowed. Empty/stopword-only query intentionally returns NONE before provider call.
Positive cosine is a candidate condition, not proof a source supports the answer; RRF scores are not confidence. No-answer candidate return rates must be reported separately.

calibrationRestrictions: No original acceptance per-question inspection, no acceptance-driven parameter selection, no change to frozen questions.
